item.title: The Amir and El-Sisi discuss investment, energy and Gaza in Cairo
item.description:
HH the Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani began an official visit to Egypt on Thursday and was received by President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi at Cairo International Airport. The two leaders held official talks at Al Ittihadiya Palace after a bilateral meeting and a luncheon, covering cooperation in investment and energy and their joint mediation to consolidate the Gaza ceasefire. The Amir was accompanied by HE Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs.
Sources: The Peninsula (QNA) https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/26/11/2026/amir-arrives-in-cairo-on-official-visit · Qatar Tribune (QNA) https://www.qatar-tribune.com/article/266624/latest-news/amir-president-of-egypt-hold-official-talks-session · Al Jazeera Net https://www.aljazeera.net/news/2026/11/26/%D8%A3%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%B1-%D9%82%D8%B7%D8%B1-%D9%8A%D8%B2%D9%88%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%82%D8%A7%D9%87%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%B3%D9%8A-%D9%81%D9%8A · Cairo Mubasher https://www.cairomubasher.com/256638

item.title: Qatar offers condolences to Egypt over the Giza fuel tanker crash
item.description:
During his talks in Cairo on Thursday, HH the Amir offered condolences over the victims of the Ring Road accident in Giza Governorate and wished the injured a speedy recovery. The Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs extended his condolences to the victims' families and to Egypt in a social media post. The accident on Wednesday evening killed 31 people after a fuel tanker hit a concrete barrier and exploded.
Sources: Qatar Tribune (QNA) https://www.qatar-tribune.com/article/266624/latest-news/amir-president-of-egypt-hold-official-talks-session · The Peninsula https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/26/11/2026/prime-minister-extends-condolences-to-families-of-egypt-traffic-accident-victims

item.title: KAHRAMAA signs over QR3bn in contracts to develop its networks
item.description:
The Qatar General Electricity and Water Corporation (KAHRAMAA) on Thursday signed contracts for strategic projects to develop electricity and water network infrastructure worth more than QR3 billion in total. Ten companies will carry out the work, five national and five international, including Larsen & Toubro and LS Cable & System. The projects also extend services to land plots allocated to citizens, said KAHRAMAA President Eng. Abdullah bin Ali Al Thiab.

item.title: Doha hosts the third session of the Arab Cybersecurity Ministers Council
item.description:
The third regular session of the Arab Cybersecurity Ministers Council opened in Doha on Thursday, with the Arab League General Secretariat and heads of national cybersecurity agencies taking part. It was opened by Eng. Abdulrahman bin Ali Al Farahid Al Malki, President of the National Cyber Security Agency. Eng. Abeer Al Awadhi, head of Kuwait's National Cyber Security Center, said the meeting aims to share information on threats and set practical strategies for each country.

item.title: Qatar condemns the attack on a Syrian Interior Ministry building in Hasakah
item.description:
Qatar on Thursday condemned the attack on a building of the Syrian Interior Ministry in Hasakah, which killed two security personnel and injured five others. In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs reaffirmed Qatar's rejection of violence and terrorism and its full solidarity with the Syrian government, and offered condolences to the families of the two victims.

item.title: Qatar renews its support for the violent-extremism prevention fund in Tokyo
item.description:
Qatar on Thursday reaffirmed its support for the Global Community Engagement and Resilience Fund (GCERF) at the Fund's 25th Board meeting in Tokyo. The delegation was led by HE Jassim bin Mohammed Al Asmakh, Special Envoy of the Minister of Foreign Affairs, who met Japan's Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs Keiichi Iwamoto on the sidelines to review bilateral cooperation and regional developments.

item.title: Kuwait: four injured by shrapnel from Iranian drones targeting a vital site
item.description:
Kuwait's Ministry of Defence said on Thursday that four people were injured and material damage caused after Iranian drones targeting an undisclosed vital site were intercepted. Spokesman Col. Saud Abdulaziz Al Atwan said forces detected the drones in Kuwaiti airspace and dealt with them. The injured, a Kuwaiti citizen, two Italians and a Pakistani, were taken to hospital.

item.title: Dubai Islamic Bank to acquire Emirates Islamic in an all-share deal
item.description:
Dubai Islamic Bank agreed to acquire Emirates Islamic from Emirates NBD in an all-share deal, creating the world's second-largest listed Islamic banking group with assets of about AED585 billion. Emirates NBD becomes a strategic shareholder through newly issued shares. Completion is subject to approval by the Central Bank of the UAE, the Capital Markets Authority and shareholders.
Sources: Arab News https://www.arabnews.com/business/dubai-islamic-bank-acquires-emirates-islamic-to-make-second-largest-islamic-banking-group-3014100 · Enterprise https://enterpriseam.com/uae/2026/11/26/dib-to-absorb-emirates-islamic-in-all-share-deal-creating-an-aed-585-bn-islamic-lender/

item.title: Sources: OPEC+ set to roll over output targets at Sunday meeting
item.description:
Two sources said on Thursday that OPEC+ may roll over its current oil output targets at its online meeting on Sunday 29 November, as the Iran war keeps disrupting exports from its Middle East members. No decision has been made. Analysts expect major quota decisions to be postponed to 2027, as the group has yet to set next year's production targets.
Sources: Business Standard (Reuters) https://www.business-standard.com/amp/world-news/opec-may-roll-over-current-oil-output-targets-at-its-sunday-meeting-126112601024_1.html · WiseVoter https://wisevoter.com/world/2026/11/26/opec-plus-weighs-rolling-over-oil-quotas-january · Newsquawk https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/opec-likely-to-roll-over-oil-output-targets-for-at-least-q1-2027-at-sundays-meeting-according-to-sources

item.title: Unknown projectile explodes near a tanker 50 nautical miles west of Dubai
item.description:
The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said on Thursday that a tanker's master reported an explosion near the vessel 50 nautical miles west of Dubai, attributing it to an unknown projectile. UKMTO said all crew were safe, with no damage or environmental impact, classed the incident as "suspicious activity" and advised ships to proceed with caution.

item.title: Houthi projectile falls at Jazan port without civilian casualties
item.description:
A projectile fell at Saudi Arabia's Jazan port, causing minor damage and no civilian casualties, after the Houthis said they had targeted the ports of Jeddah and Jazan in retaliation for coalition strikes on Hodeidah port. The coalition destroyed two drones over the Eastern Province, spokesman Maj Gen Turki Al Malki said.
Sources: The National https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/gulf/2026/11/26/saudi-arabia-intercepts-wave-of-retaliatory-houthi-attacks/ · The Diplomatic Insight https://thediplomaticinsight.com/saudi-coalition-intercepts-two-houthi-missiles/

item.title: El-Sisi tells Qatar's Amir that Gulf security is part of Egypt's national security
item.description:
President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi affirmed Egypt's full support for the security of Qatar and the Gulf states during talks with Qatar's Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani at Al Ittihadiya Palace on Thursday. Presidency spokesman Ambassador Mohamed El-Shennawy said the president stressed raising trade and expanding cooperation in investment and energy. The talks covered implementing the Gaza ceasefire agreement and de-escalation in the region.

item.title: Health Ministry: final toll of Warraq Ring Road crash is 31 dead, 26 injured
item.description:
The Ministry of Health and Population on Thursday announced the final toll of the petroleum tanker fire on the Ring Road in Warraq, Giza: 31 dead and 26 injured. Twenty-one of the injured remain in treatment, eight were transferred to the burns unit at Sheikh Zayed Al Nahyan Hospital, and five were discharged after improving. The ministry sent 39 ambulances to the scene.

item.title: Prosecutors detain a driver suspected of causing the fuel tanker disaster
item.description:
The Public Prosecution said on Thursday it had detained a driver suspected of causing the petroleum tanker accident on the Ring Road in Warraq. The suspect admitted he was driving with his father at 110 km/h and hit the rear of the tanker while overtaking, after which one of its tyres burst, it overturned and petrol leaked. Twenty-seven vehicles were burned out, and prosecutors ordered DNA samples from unidentified bodies.

item.title: Washington proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners
item.description:
The US Trade Representative proposed new tariffs on goods from 14 trading partners, including China, the European Union, Japan, India and South Korea, after an eight-month probe into excess industrial capacity. China faces an additional 20% levy, and other partners between 10% and 18%. The rates will be published in the Federal Register, with implementation likely in January at the earliest.
Sources: RTÉ (AFP/Reuters) https://www.rte.ie/news/us/2026/1125/1600630-us-tariffs/ · ABC News (Australia) https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-26/trump-new-tariffs-major-trading-partners/107425504 · Yahoo Finance (New York Post) https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/us-proposes-tariffs-14-trading-133756472.html

item.title: Israeli strikes kill nine Palestinians in Gaza for a third night
item.description:
Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians in Gaza overnight into Thursday, including Khaled Abu Nada, the Hamas-appointed deputy education minister, and his wife in Deir Al-Balah, medics said. Two other strikes killed six people in the Tuffah neighbourhood and Beach camp. At least 1,600 Palestinians and five Israeli soldiers have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire.
Sources: Business Recorder (Reuters) https://www.brecorder.com/news/40450867/israel-kills-nine-in-gaza-including-a-hamas-appointed-minister-officials-say · ClickOnDetroit (AP) https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/world/2026/11/26/israeli-strikes-kill-8-in-gaza-and-other-mideast-news/

item.title: Russian missile and drone barrage kills three in Ukraine
item.description:
Russia fired ballistic missiles and 113 drones at Kyiv and seven Ukrainian regions overnight into Thursday, killing two people in Kharkiv and a third in the Kyiv region, and injuring seven in the capital. Ukrainian air defences downed 87 aerial targets. The strikes hit water facilities, heating networks and shopping centres, and two foreign vessels carrying more than 100,000 tonnes of grain were attacked near Odesa.
Sources: Euronews https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/26/russia-launches-ballistic-missile-and-drone-barrage-on-ukraine-killing-at-least-three · LB.ua https://en.lb.ua/news/2026/11/26/51574_overnight_russian_strikes_hit.html

item.title: Global stocks rise while US markets close for Thanksgiving
item.description:
European and Asian shares rose on Thursday as technology stocks rebounded and US markets closed for Thanksgiving. Germany's DAX rose 1.9% to 25,180.12 points in early trading, France's CAC 40 1.8% and Britain's FTSE 100 1.6%. Japan's Nikkei closed 0.9% higher at 57,499.16 points, and Wall Street reopens on Friday for a shortened session.

item.title: Brent eases to $93.79 after sharp gains a day earlier
item.description:
Brent crude fell 82 cents, or 0.87%, to $93.79 a barrel at 0939 GMT after rising 3.5% a day earlier, when the Houthis said they attacked the Ras Tanura refinery and Iran said tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. US crude fell 0.42% to $83.33, with no settlement on Thursday due to Thanksgiving. US crude stocks rose 1.1 million barrels.

item.title: Turkey's central bank suspends purchases of domestically mined gold
item.description:
Turkey's central bank suspended purchases of gold produced from domestic mines from Thursday until further notice, according to banking sources, with no official statement on the reason or duration. The move covers only standard domestic gold; a similar suspension was imposed in October 2025 and lifted in March 2026. Spot gold steadied at $3,580.87 in the morning after dropping below $3,500 on Wednesday.
